newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares recover at close after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares recover at close after Greenspan.

text.p: 1740 GMT - Portuguese shares recovered at the close after a brief sell-off provoked by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's warning about financial markets overheating. "Tomorrow the market should fall again, if sentiment abroad remains negative after Greenspan's warning over inflation," said one operator.

* The most active shares included Banco Portugues de Investimento whose shares sank four percent as it disappointed investors with a 56 percent rise in 1996 profit. BPI boosted its 1996 profit to 15.1 billion escudos ($90 million) from 9.7 billion in 1995.

* Ship repairer Lisnave recovered after taking a beating in recent sessions following its announcement that it would drastically reduce its capital as part of a restructuring programme. It closed at 358 escudos, up 17, in turnover of 226,359 shares.

* Portucel recovered as its 1.4 billion escudos 1996 loss was a better than expected result and the market was optimistic about the restructuring of the pulp sector, dealers said. It closed at 994 escudos, up four.
